On Mon, Feb 1, 2016 at 10:31 PM, Seth Madlon-Kay <seth.ma...@gmail.com> wrote:
Greetings Stan Team,

I noticed that RStan does not set the length of the adaptation phases to match the warmup length specified in the function call the way CmdStan does. This results in mass matrix never being tuned in runs with shorter warmups. Perhaps this is a known issue, but I didn't see anything relating to this on GitHub.

testcode <- 'parameters { real y;}
  model{ y ~ normal(0,1);}'
test <- stan_model(model_code=testcode)
sampling(test,iter=200,warmup=149,chains=1,diagnostic_file="testdiag.csv")
readLines("testdiag.csv")[175:176]
[1] "# Diagonal elements of inverse mass matrix:"
[2] "# 1"                                        

If warmup is at least as long as the sum of the default adaptation phase lengths listed in the 'stan' function R documentation, it seems adaptation goes as intended (well, at least in that mass matrix tuning begins):
sampling(test,iter=200,warmup=150,chains=1,diagnostic_file="testdiag.csv")
readLines("testdiag.csv")[176:177]
[1] "# Diagonal elements of inverse mass matrix:"
[2] "# 0.508071"
 
If you manually specify the lengths of the phases to match the the warmup, you also get the correct behavior:
sampling(test,iter=200,warmup=149,chains=1,diagnostic_file="testdiag.csv",
         control=list(adapt_init_buffer=25,adapt_window=100,adapt_term_buffer=24))
readLines("testdiag.csv")[175:176]
[1] "# Diagonal elements of inverse mass matrix:"
[2] "# 1.47892"                                  
I've reproduced this issue in R version 3.2.3 in RStudio 0.99.491 on Ubuntu 15.10 and Windows 7, and on the R terminal in Windows 7, all 64 bit.

-Seth
